source.syllabus: NTA, Syllabus for JEE (Main) 2026, Paper 1 Mathematics, Unit 2: quadratic equations in real and complex number systems and their solutions; relations between roots and coefficients; nature of roots; formation of quadratic equations with given roots.
source.marking: NTA, Information Bulletin JEE (Main) 2026: Section A multiple choice and Section B numerical value, +4 correct, -1 incorrect, 0 unanswered; numerical answers are integers.

screens.title: The standard form
text: A quadratic equation is an equation that can be written as
with a, b, c real numbers and a ≠ 0. The highest power of x is 2: that is what “quadratic” means.

screens.title: Examples
text: 3x² − 12 = 0 (b = 0 is allowed)
x(x − 3) = 4 is quadratic too: expand it to x² − 3x − 4 = 0.
screens.tip: Always rewrite in standard form first. Then read off a, b and c, signs included.

screens.title: What a root is
text: A root is a value of x that makes the equation true.
Try x = 2 in x² − 5x + 6:
So 2 is a root. Check for yourself that 3 is the other root.

screens.title: The picture: a parabola
text: The graph of y = ax² + bx + c is a U-shaped curve called a parabola (upside down when a < 0).
The roots are exactly where the curve meets the x-axis (where y = 0). Here: at x = 2 and x = 3.

screens.title: Key fact
text: A quadratic equation has exactly two roots (counting complex numbers, and counting a repeated root twice). It can never have three.
So if a question gives you three different numbers that all satisfy ax² + bx + c = 0, then a = b = c = 0: it was never a quadratic.

screens.title: The zero-product rule
text: If two numbers multiply to give 0, at least one of them is 0.
So once you write the quadratic as a product of two brackets, each bracket gives a root.

screens.title: Splitting the middle term (a = 1)
text: For x² − 5x + 6 = 0, find two numbers whose product is c = 6 and whose sum is b = −5.
They are −2 and −3.

screens.title: When a ≠ 1
text: Solve 2x² + 5x − 3 = 0. Now look for two numbers with product a × c = −6 and sum b = 5: they are 6 and −1.

screens.title: A classic mistake
text: Solve x² = 3x. Dividing both sides by x gives x = 3 and loses a root.
Instead bring everything to one side: x² − 3x = 0, so x(x − 3) = 0, and x = 0 or x = 3.
screens.tip: Never divide by an expression that could be zero. Factor it out instead.

lessons.title: Completing the square and the formula

screens.title: Completing the square
text: Not every quadratic factorises nicely. Completing the square always works.
Solve x² + 6x + 5 = 0. Half of 6 is 3, and (x + 3)² = x² + 6x + 9.

screens.title: Doing it in general
text: Do the same steps to ax² + bx + c = 0: divide by a, move c/a across, and add (b/2a)² to both sides.

screens.title: The quadratic formula
text: This gives both roots of every quadratic equation:
The expression under the root, b² − 4ac, is called the discriminant, D. The next lesson is all about it.

screens.title: Using it
screens.tip: Simplify the surd and cancel the common factor. JEE options are usually written in the simplest form.

lessons.title: The discriminant and the nature of roots

screens.title: D tells you the type of roots
text: Before solving, D = b² − 4ac tells you what kind of roots to expect:
D > 0: two different real roots.
D = 0: two equal real roots, both x = −b/2a.
D < 0: no real roots; the roots are two complex conjugates (lesson 7).

screens.title: See it on the graph
text: Move the sliders. Watch where the parabola meets the x-axis and how the sign of D changes: two crossings, one touch, or no meeting point.

screens.title: Rational or irrational?
text: If a, b and c are rational (for example integers) and D is a perfect square, the roots are rational.
If D > 0 is not a perfect square, the roots are irrational and come as a pair p ± √q.

screens.title: A JEE favourite: equal roots
text: For what values of k does x² + kx + 9 = 0 have equal roots?
Equal roots means D = 0.
screens.tip: “Equal roots” → D = 0. “Real roots” → D ≥ 0. “Real and distinct” → D > 0. “No real roots” → D < 0.

screens.title: Read them off the coefficients
text: If α and β are the roots of ax² + bx + c = 0, then:
Add the two values from the quadratic formula: the ±√D parts cancel and leave −2b/2a. Multiplying them gives (b² − D)/4a² = c/a.

screens.title: Example
text: For 2x² − 3x − 5 = 0:
screens.tip: Watch the minus sign in −b/a. Getting it wrong is the most common slip.

screens.title: Symmetric expressions
text: Many JEE questions ask for an expression in α and β without finding α and β. Rewrite it using only α + β and αβ:

screens.title: Try the method
text: α, β are the roots of x² − 3x + 1 = 0. Then α + β = 3 and αβ = 1, so
screens.tip: Notice that we never found α or β (they are (3 ± √5)/2). That is the point: it is faster and avoids messy surds.

lessons.title: Forming an equation from its roots

screens.title: The rule
text: A quadratic with roots α and β is
Read it as: x² − (sum of roots)x + (product of roots) = 0.

screens.title: Examples
text: Roots 3 and −5: sum −2, product −15.
Roots 1 + √2 and 1 − √2: sum 2, product 1 − 2 = −1.

screens.title: New roots from old ones
text: α, β are the roots of x² − 3x + 1 = 0. Find the equation whose roots are α² and β².
New sum = α² + β² = 7 (from the last lesson). New product = (αβ)² = 1.
screens.tip: For roots 1/α and 1/β, just swap a and c: from ax² + bx + c = 0 you get cx² + bx + a = 0.

screens.title: When D < 0
text: There is no real number whose square is negative, so we use i, where i² = −1. Then √(−4) = 2i.
x² + 4 = 0 gives x² = −4, so x = 2i or x = −2i.

screens.title: Conjugate pairs
text: When a, b and c are real, complex roots always come in a pair p + qi and p − qi (complex conjugates).
Sum = 2p and product = p² + q², so the sum and product rules still work.
screens.tip: If a question says one root of a real quadratic is 2 + 3i, you already know the other one: 2 − 3i.

screens.title: Substitution
text: Some equations are quadratics in disguise. In x⁴ − 5x² + 4 = 0, put t = x²:
t = 1 gives x = ±1 and t = 4 gives x = ±2: four real solutions.

screens.title: With a modulus
text: Solve x² − 5|x| + 6 = 0. Since x² = |x|², put t = |x| (and remember t ≥ 0):
|x| = 2 gives x = ±2 and |x| = 3 gives x = ±3: four solutions.

screens.title: Check what t is allowed to be
text: After a substitution, throw away any value of t that is impossible.
In x⁴ + x² − 6 = 0, t = x² gives t = 2 or t = −3. But x² can never be −3, so only x = ±√2 are real solutions.
screens.tip: t = x² and t = |x| must be ≥ 0. Count the solutions carefully: JEE often asks how many there are.

formulaSheet.title: The standard form
formulaSheet.text: A quadratic equation is ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0. It always has two roots, α and β, in the complex numbers (they may be equal).

formulaSheet.title: The formula
formulaSheet.text: α, β = (−b ± √D) / 2a, where D = b² − 4ac is the discriminant.

formulaSheet.title: Nature of roots
formulaSheet.text: D > 0: two different real roots. D = 0: two equal real roots. D < 0: two non-real roots, complex conjugates p ± qi (for real a, b, c).

formulaSheet.title: Sum and product
formulaSheet.text: α + β = −b/a and αβ = c/a. You can often answer without finding α and β at all.

formulaSheet.title: Useful identities
formulaSheet.text: α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ.   α³ + β³ = (α + β)³ − 3αβ(α + β).   (α − β)² = (α + β)² − 4αβ.

formulaSheet.title: Building an equation
formulaSheet.text: With roots α and β: x² − (α + β)x + αβ = 0. Multiply through to clear fractions.

stages.title: Worked example
stages.problem: α and β are the roots of x² − 4x + 1 = 0. Find α³ + β³.
steps: Do not solve for α and β. Read the sum and product from the coefficients: a = 1, b = −4, c = 1.
Answer: 52. A numerical-value question would want the integer 52, and the same idea works for α² + β², 1/α + 1/β and α⁴ + β⁴.

questions.prompt: Which one of these is a quadratic equation?
questions.hint: Expand and bring everything to one side before deciding.
questions.solution: x(x − 3) = 4 becomes x² − 3x − 4 = 0, degree 2. (x + 1)² = x² looks quadratic but simplifies to 2x + 1 = 0, which is linear.

questions.prompt: Find the larger root of x² − 7x + 12 = 0.
questions.hint: Two numbers with product 12 and sum −7.
questions.solution: x² − 7x + 12 = (x − 3)(x − 4), so the roots are 3 and 4. The larger is 4.

questions.prompt: The roots of x² − 2x − 1 = 0 are
questions.hint: a = 1, b = −2, c = −1. Find D first.

questions.prompt: Find the positive value of k for which x² − kx + 25 = 0 has equal roots.
questions.solution: D = k² − 100 = 0, so k = ±10. The positive value is 10.

questions.prompt: α and β are the roots of x² − 4x + 2 = 0. Find α² + β².
The quadratic equation with roots 2 and −3 is
questions.solution: Sum = −1 and product = −6, so x² − (−1)x + (−6) = x² + x − 6 = 0.

questions.prompt: One root of x² + bx + c = 0, with b and c real, is 3 + i. Then (b, c) is
questions.hint: The other root is the conjugate 3 − i.
questions.solution: The roots are 3 ± i: sum 6 and product 9 + 1 = 10. So x² − 6x + 10 = 0, giving b = −6 and c = 10.

questions.prompt: How many real solutions does x⁴ − 10x² + 9 = 0 have?
questions.solution: t² − 10t + 9 = 0 gives t = 1 or t = 9. Then x = ±1 and x = ±3: four real solutions.

questions.prompt: α and β are the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0. Find α² + β².
questions.hint: α + β = 5 and αβ = 6. Use α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ.

questions.prompt: The roots of 2x² − 4x + 5 = 0 are:
questions.solution: D = (−4)² − 4 × 2 × 5 = 16 − 40 = −24 < 0, so the roots are non-real complex conjugates. (With real coefficients, non-real roots always come in a conjugate pair, so D is never 'one real, one non-real'.)

questions.prompt: For k > 0, x² + kx + 16 = 0 has equal roots. Find k.
The quadratic equation whose roots are 2 + √3 and 2 − √3 is:
questions.hint: Find the sum and the product of the two roots.
questions.solution: Sum = 4, product = (2 + √3)(2 − √3) = 4 − 3 = 1. The equation is x² − 4x + 1 = 0.

questions.prompt: α and β are the roots of x² − 3x + 1 = 0. Find α³ + β³.
questions.hint: α³ + β³ = (α + β)³ − 3αβ(α + β), with α + β = 3 and αβ = 1.

questions.prompt: The roots of x² − (k + 1)x + k = 0 differ by 3, and k > 1. Then k equals:
questions.hint: Try x = 1 in the equation. Then the other root is the product divided by 1.
questions.solution: x = 1 is a root (1 − k − 1 + k = 0), so the other root is k (the product). k − 1 = 3 gives k = 4.

questions.prompt: α and β are the roots of x² + 4x − 5 = 0. Find |α − β|.
The roots of x² − 2kx + 9 = 0 are real exactly when:
questions.solution: D = 4k² − 36 ≥ 0 gives k² ≥ 9, that is |k| ≥ 3 (k ≤ −3 also works).

questions.prompt: α and β are the roots of 2x² − 6x + 3 = 0. Find 1/α + 1/β.
The quadratic equation with roots 3 and −1/2 is:
If α and β are the roots of x² − 6x + 4 = 0, then α²β + αβ² equals:
questions.solution: α²β + αβ² = αβ(α + β) = 4 × 6 = 24.

questions.prompt: The number of real roots of x² − 5|x| + 6 = 0 is:
questions.solution: Let t = |x| ≥ 0: t² − 5t + 6 = 0 gives t = 2 or 3, so x = ±2, ±3: four real roots.

questions.prompt: x² + 2(k − 1)x + (k + 5) = 0 has equal roots. The sum of all possible values of k is:
questions.solution: D = 4(k − 1)² − 4(k + 5) = 0 gives k² − 3k − 4 = 0, so k = 4 or k = −1. Their sum is 3.

questions.prompt: The roots of x² − 2x + 2 = 0 are:
α and β are the roots of x² − x − 1 = 0. Find α⁴ + β⁴. (Numerical value: enter an integer.)
questions.solution: α² + β² = 1 + 2 = 3. Then α⁴ + β⁴ = (α² + β²)² − 2(αβ)² = 9 − 2 = 7.

questions.prompt: α and β are the roots of x² − 7x + 10 = 0. Find α² + β².
The roots of x² + 6x + 9 = 0 are:
questions.solution: D = 36 − 36 = 0: two equal real roots (both −3).
